hints: Focus on what type of reaction forms a cyanohydrin from an aldehyde, and which species acts as the nucleophile.
Remember oxygen is more electronegative than carbon, so check which end of the C=O bond is delta positive and delta negative.
Check the direction of every curly arrow, a lone pair or pi bond must donate to an electron-deficient atom, and the O- intermediate must donate to H+.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction**

This is nucleophilic addition of HCN to propanal to form a cyanohydrin.

Starting aldehyde:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH(CN)O}^-$$

**Check the carbonyl polarity**

Oxygen is more electronegative than carbon, so it pulls the pi electrons toward itself.

Correct polarity is:
$$\text{C}^{\delta+} = \text{O}^{\delta-}$$

**Check the first nucleophilic attack**

The nucleophile $\text{CN}^-$ uses its lone pair to attack the electron-deficient $\text{C}^{\delta+}$.

At the same time the C=O pi bond breaks and both electrons move onto oxygen to give $\text{O}^-$.

So both curly arrows must start from an electron pair and point toward the electron-deficient centre.

**Check the protonation step**

The intermediate alkoxide ion $\text{O}^-$ is a base and uses its lone pair to attract $\text{H}^+$.

Correct arrow is:
$$\text{O}^- \rightarrow \text{H}^+$$
This forms $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH(OH)(CN)}$. Only one mechanism gets all the dipoles and both arrow directions right.

options.A: First step dipoles and attack by CN- on C delta+ are correct, but the second step arrow is reversed. It shows H+ donating to O-, when the lone pair on O- must donate to H+. Curly arrows must flow from electron-rich to electron-poor.
options.B: Second step protonation arrow is correct, but the first step nucleophilic attack arrow is reversed. It points away from the carbonyl carbon toward CN-, which would imply the carbonyl is donating to cyanide. The nucleophile CN- must donate to the carbonyl C delta+.
options.C: The carbonyl dipoles are the wrong way round, showing C delta- and O delta+. This contradicts electronegativity since oxygen is more electronegative than carbon. CN- would not attack a delta- carbon.
options.D: All details are correct. C is delta+ and O is delta-, CN- donates its lone pair to C delta+, the C=O pi electrons move onto O to give O-, and then O- donates its lone pair to H+ to give the cyanohydrin C2H5CH(OH)(CN).
